items.title: Anwar's 'sane people' jab lands as questions swirl over Trump
items.description: The world is stuck watching a performative series of announcements about meetings that could, may, will happen, involving a president not dealing with the reality that he is in a weak and confused bargaining position.

items.title: Live: Iran, Trump clash over US blockade during peace talks
items.description: US President Donald Trump says he intends to keep up his naval blockade of Iran until a peace agreement is signed, putting him at odds with Iran's foreign ministry, which says the blockade is a breach of the US's ceasefire commitments. Follow live.

items.title: Why global stocks keep heading into orbit
items.description: The Australian Securities Exchange is within striking distance of new records as economists issue worst-case warnings of a close call for a global recession.

items.title: The PM is not about to pick a fight over a gas tax
items.description: The budget's usual timing on the second Tuesday of May is an artifice of political convention. This year's edition just happens to be coinciding with the thunderclap of history in flux.

items.title: Winners and losers emerge in volatile airfare market
items.description: Australians are finding domestic flights for as little as $65 on some routes, while others are paying thousands to travel interstate as airlines quietly reshape the market in response to conflict in the Middle East.

items.title: Harry and Meghan seek duty and dollars on tour
items.description: Mixing philanthropy, influencing and brand building, Harry and Meghan’s Australian tour revives a question Queen Elizabeth once shut down: can the 'half in, half out' royal life work?

items.title: Outcry over 'disturbing' video of off-duty police officer pinning 13yo girl on train
items.description: Video of an off-duty police officer restraining a 13yo girl on a Perth train has sparked accusations of excessive force.

items.title: An executive at FIFA's new betting partner settled an insider-trading lawsuit
items.description: The backstory of the prediction market industry's newest entrant has done little to calm concerns as it partners with several giants of sports broadcasting.

items.title: As Trump spruiks Lebanon ceasefire, some want war to continue
items.description: Donald Trump sold a ceasefire in Lebanon as a step towards peace. But that promise hinges on a condition that Lebanon may not be able to deliver.

items.title: Desperate for social media ban to work, but parents say it’s 'impossible'
items.description: Tech companies are coming under fire as Australian parents increasingly voice concerns that some online platforms are failing to keep kids under 16 off their platforms.

items.title: Not all city suburbs have NBN access and it isn't by accident. Here's why
items.description: Despite popular belief, not all Australians are guaranteed access to the NBN — and as many consumers have discovered, alternative networks do not always provide quality service.

items.title: Australia enters drone warfare era with Ghost Bat and Ghost Shark
items.description: Australia is on a push to keep pace with the rapid evolution of drone warfare, with an emphasis on locally produced Ghost Bat and Ghost Shark systems.

items.title: How lawyers are using AI, and financial planners aren't far behind
items.description: Businesses say they are using AI to speed up service delivery and improve the customer experience, but economists warn this may be the "calm before the storm".

items.title: The 'immense complexity' facing Ben Roberts-Smith's prosecutors
items.description: A legal expert says the criminal prosecution of former soldier Ben Roberts-Smith will test Australia's war crimes legal framework in ways never seen before, as the case moves toward a trial.

items.title: National 'Walk for Truth' asks PM to deliver on long-awaited promise
items.description: Indigenous leader Travis Lovett sets off on a trek to Canberra, calling for action from the federal government to support a national truth-telling process for First Nations people.

items.title: Oil prices plunge after news Strait of Hormuz to open
items.description: Oil prices plunged more than 10 per cent after Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz would be "completely open" but shipping giants are approaching the situation with caution.

items.title: Do acupuncture and herbs actually help with menopause symptoms?
items.description: Complementary therapies may help some menopausal symptoms, but more high-quality research is needed to understand how effective and safe these treatments truly are.

items.title: Inside the legal feud between Gina Rinehart and Angela Bennett
items.description: Their fathers were school buddies turned mining pioneers, and in another life they could have been friends — but Gina Rinehart and Angela Bennett came to be opponents in one of the most high-stakes legal battles Australia has ever seen.

items.title: Patients with little-known neurological condition wait years for diagnosis
items.description: People with functional neurological disorder say they experience misdiagnosis and struggles within the medical system.

items.title: Amid misogynistic criticism, Marie-Louise Eta is set to break new ground
items.description: Amid a storm of misogynistic criticism, Marie-Louise Eta will become the first woman to take charge of a men's football team in one of Europe's top five leagues. But she just wants everyone to focus on the football.

items.title: The Aussie farmer making waves in Kenya
items.description: After moving to Kenya 15 years ago Aussie farmer Stuart Barden's dream has become reality. The 55-year-old is helping change the face of the country's cropping industry.

items.title: Two words threaten to derail Minns's plan to ban controversial phrase
items.description: NSW Premier Chris Minns must now decide whether to proceed with the next restrictions he hoped to impose on protests after his latest court defeat.

items.title: New scooters and e-bikes have arrived in Canberra. Here's what that means
items.description: With Neuron's orange scooters having left Canberra, Lime has introduced a fleet of green scooters and e-bikes across the capital in partnership with the ACT government.

items.title: 'Derek' the dingo a concern for some as he roams streets in outback town
items.description: An lone dingo, affectionately known as Derek, has been spotted in suburban streets, backyards and even in dog parks, raising some concern for Alice Springs residents.

items.title: Fremantle Prison break remembered 150 years on as 'ultimate story' of hope and freedom
items.description: The story of how a Fenian captain from Massachusetts defied the odds and rescued six Irish political convicts from a prison on the very edge of the world.
